query: Why do some Amazon products receive predominantly negative reviews, and which factors contribute the most?

per_column.name: product_quality_defect_mentioned
per_column.rationale: Categorising types of quality/defect complaints gives a genuine grouping axis for the 'which factors contribute most' query. The sampled rows are all non-defect complaints (book, music, doll availability) and were correctly marked not_present, showing sound reading of source text.

per_column.name: performance_inadequacy_type
per_column.rationale: Distinguishing works_poorly / does_not_work / insufficient provides a distinct performance-failure axis useful for identifying negative-review drivers. Sampled silent rows correctly labelled not_present; no invented specifics observed.

per_column.name: value_for_money_concern
per_column.rationale: Captures price/value dissatisfaction as a separate contributing factor, directly relevant to why products get negative reviews. Sample rows without price complaints correctly marked not_present; values are warranted readings.

judge.rationale: The three added columns each provide a distinct, non-redundant categorical axis (quality/defect, performance, value) that directly supports analysing and ranking factors behind negative reviews. Values in the evidence samples are sound readings of the source text, with silent rows appropriately marked not_present rather than fabricated. No hallucination observed in samples. Only mild concern is that the categories rely on inference from free text, but the observed behaviour is well grounded.
